notes:
Initial discovery: product org of ~1.5k engs building an in-IDE copilot (IDE plugins for VS Code & JetBrains). Primary ask = low-latency token streaming for completions and multi-file code actions.

Key requirements / raw snippets from calls:
- Latency target: 50-120ms token latency for completions (hot paths).
- Throughput: thousands of concurrent active devs at peak -> need predictable p99 and autoscale.
- Cost sensitivity: CFO/FinOps wants per-seat economics; target blended unit cost <$0.03/active-hour (engineering definition).
- Model/version pinning: dev teams want stable pinned model for prod release trains + ability to roll forward for beta groups.
- Caching: heavy reuse of common prefixes (boilerplate), interested in prefix/KV caching and cache shard strategy.
- Quantization profiles: want recommended quant profiles per workload (fast completions vs high-quality refactors).

Quotes: "We can trade small accuracy delta for 4-6x cost win on hot paths." — Lead ML Eng.

Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, org-wide audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and EU code residency for certain teams. Legal asked for a data retention policy variant for ephemeral cache TTLs.

POC summary: running 2-week POC on Redwood Dedicated; SE provided perf harness. POC goals: p50/p95 token latency, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit rate >40% on prefix cache for common completions, quantized model accuracy delta <4% vs baseline.

POC results (first pass):
- Dedicated cluster hit baseline latencies (p50 within target), p95 spikes during burst.
- Quantized 7B reduced token cost ~3.8x but small regressions for complex refactors.
- Cache reduced token throughput by ~28% (early numbers), suggests room to tune shard size / TTL.

Internal stakeholders: CTO (ops risk), Head of Dev Platforms (sponsor), Lead ML Eng (technical champion), FinOps (pricing model owner).

Open asks to Redwood:
- Clear per-seat pricing scenarios (dedicated reserved + burst) and unit math samples for 1k / 5k / 10k active devs.
- Deeper docs on quantization profiles (latency vs accuracy tradeoff) and recommended rollout strategy for model pinning (canary -> org rollouts).
- Guidance on cache sizing and eviction strategy for multi-tenant IDE workloads.
- SLA language for p95 latency and fallback policies if dedicated capacity is saturated.

Short-term next steps: SE to run quantization A/B (week of 3/16), AE to send SOW draft, Legal to review residency clause by 3/24.
